references.title: NE 100 — Introduction to Neural Engineering
references.notes: Curriculum baseline spanning neuroanatomy/neurophysiology, monitoring technologies, neural replacement/restoration devices, imaging, and computational approaches.

references.title: Neural Engineering, BS
references.notes: Program-level baseline showing the field's integration of neuroscience, electrical and imaging systems, molecular/cellular engineering, biological interfacing, neural data science, design, regulation, and ethics.

references.title: About the BRAIN Initiative
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Authoritative current framing of neurotechnology development as a means to understand dynamic brain activity across cells and circuits and to advance research and clinical capabilities.

references.title: Neural Recording and Modulation
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Current authoritative map of recording and modulation technology, including electrical, optical, magnetic, acoustic, molecular, genetic, ASIC, adaptive-optics, and signal-processing components.

references.title: BRAIN 2025: A Scientific Vision
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Strategic baseline for large-scale monitoring, human neural technology, integrated measurement and perturbation, biocompatibility, chronic reliability, neural interfaces, theory, modeling, statistics, and translational goals.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.4 The Action Potential
references.notes: Open textbook foundation for membrane potential, ionic gradients, voltage-gated channels, action potentials, threshold, repolarization, and refractory behavior.

references.title: Neurological Devices
references.notes: Current regulatory overview establishing diagnostic, neurointerventional, neurostimulation, sensory-restoration, prosthetic, safety, and market-access context.

references.title: Implanted Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Devices for Patients with Paralysis or Amputation — Non-clinical Testing and Clinical Considerations
references.notes: Authoritative translational baseline for implanted BCI nonclinical testing, IDE study design, device reliability, biocompatibility, electrical safety, wireless technology, MRI compatibility, and clinical considerations.

references.title: BRAIN 2.0 Neuroethics: Enabling and Enhancing Neuroscience Advances for Society
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Neuroethics baseline for closed-loop monitoring/stimulation and questions involving privacy, agency, identity, autonomy, consent, social context, and responsible innovation.

references.title: Brain-computer interfaces: Definitions and principles
references.authority: Jonathan R. Wolpaw, José del R. Millán, Nick F. Ramsey
references.notes: Foundational BCI definition emphasizing measurement of CNS activity and translation into artificial outputs that replace, restore, enhance, supplement, or improve natural CNS outputs.

references.title: Standards and Guidances for Neurological Devices
references.notes: Current FDA entry point for neurological-device standards and guidance, including biocompatibility and other safety/effectiveness considerations.

references.title: Therapeutic Human Neuroscience Program
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Current translational program baseline for FDA-regulated invasive and noninvasive CNS technologies, including closed-loop sensing and stimulation.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.1 Basic Structure and Function of the Nervous System
references.notes: Primary L0 source for anatomical CNS/PNS divisions, sensation-integration-response, and somatic/autonomic/enteric functional organization.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 13.2 The Central Nervous System
references.notes: Foundation for the major adult brain regions and the spinal cord as both a communication pathway and an integration site.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Chapter 13 Review
references.notes: Compact source for peripheral nervous system structure, including ganglia, cranial/spinal nerves, and mixed sensory/motor fibers.

references.title: Neuroscience — Neural Systems
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Foundational systems-neuroscience map linking CNS/PNS anatomy, sensory pathways, somatic motor output, autonomic output, and distributed neural systems.
